Reproduce the ACS manuscript-style validation plots for StimGate, $F_{\beta}$ and
Tailgate using the comparison table produced by the main ACS analysis.
The figures use saved results from Analysis 9b without rerunning the gating
methods. Tailgate uses the configuration Analysis 9a selected against these
manual references, so its agreement here is in-sample.

## Set-up

Failed method/marker estimates remain missing and are excluded from agreement
statistics; correlation tables state total, failed and scored counts for each
included stratum. Analysis 9b also saves coverage for all strata and an exclusion
table for unmatched cohort keys.

The saved `acs_cytof/manual-comparison/manual-comparison.rds` table is sufficient for frequency and correlation plots. The F₁ heatmaps also read the prepared population GatingSets from `acs_cytof/gs`; raw FCS files are not needed here. Render Analyses 9a and 9b with `RUN_SIMULATIONS=true RUN_PLOTS=false` first if that table is missing. `RUN_PLOTS=true` displays and saves the validation figures; this document does not rerun the gating methods.

```{r}
#| label: setup
#| include: false
library(ggplot2)
library(dplyr)

root_dir <- normalizePath(if (file.exists("DESCRIPTION")) "." else "..", winslash = "/")
stopifnot(file.exists(file.path(root_dir, "DESCRIPTION")))
knitr::opts_knit$set(root.dir = root_dir)

scripts_r_dir <- file.path(root_dir, "scripts", "r")
source(file.path(scripts_r_dir, "analysis-runtime.R"))
source(file.path(scripts_r_dir, "analysis-plot-style.R"))
source(file.path(scripts_r_dir, "analysis-thesis-table.R"))
source(file.path(scripts_r_dir, "analysis-mcse.R"))
source(file.path(scripts_r_dir, "sim-bandwidth-analysis-plot.R"))
fig_key <- .analysis_mode_key("10-real-compare-acs-cytof-validation", sized = FALSE)
source(file.path(scripts_r_dir, "acs_cytof-helper.R"))
source(file.path(scripts_r_dir, "acs_cytof-gate.R"))
source(file.path(scripts_r_dir, "acs_cytof-manual.R"))
source(file.path(scripts_r_dir, "acs_cytof-plot_cyt.R"))
source(file.path(scripts_r_dir, "acs_cytof-ccc-summary.R"))
source(file.path(scripts_r_dir, "acs_cytof-scatter-stacked.R"))
source(file.path(scripts_r_dir, "acs_cytof-scatter-alt.R"))
source(file.path(scripts_r_dir, "acs_cytof-f1.R"))
.analysis_method_labels[c("fbeta", "fbeta_default")] <-
  .acsCytofValidationMethodLabels()[c("fbeta", "fbeta_default")]
source(file.path(scripts_r_dir, "acs_cytof-methods.R"))
source(file.path(scripts_r_dir, "acs_cytof-tailgate-select.R"))

run_simulations <- .as_flag(.get_qmd_param_env(
  "run_simulations",
  "RUN_SIMULATIONS",
  FALSE
))
run_plots <- .as_flag(.get_qmd_param_env(
  "run_plots",
  "RUN_PLOTS",
  TRUE
))

path_manual_output <- projr::projr_path_get(
  "cache",
  "acs_cytof",
  "manual-comparison",
  format = "absolute"
)
path_comparison <- file.path(
  path_manual_output,
  "manual-comparison.rds"
)
# Must match the StimGate threshold method set in Analysis 9b.
stimgate_loc_threshold_method <- "cap"
qmd_9b <- "analysis/9b-real-compare-acs-cytof.qmd"
manual_run_manifest <- .analysis_read_rds(
  file.path(path_manual_output, "manifest.rds"), "acs_cytof", qmd_9b
)
.analysis_check_expected_run(
  manual_run_manifest,
  "acs_cytof", qmd_9b,
  semantics_version = "acs-cytof-v10"
)
.acsCytofCheckRunManifestMethod(
  manual_run_manifest, stimgate_loc_threshold_method, qmd_9b
)
# Tailgate's results must come from the configuration 9a currently selects.
tailgate_selection <- .acsCytofReadTailgateSelection(
  .acsCytofTailgateSelectionDir(root_dir)
)
.acsCytofCheckRunManifestTailgate(manual_run_manifest, tailgate_selection, qmd_9b)
manual_comparison_tbl <- .analysis_read_rds(path_comparison, "acs_cytof", qmd_9b)
.acsCytofValidateComparisonManifest(
  manual_comparison_tbl,
  locThresholdMethod = stimgate_loc_threshold_method
)
validation_methods <- .acsCytofValidationMethods()
appendix_methods <- .acsCytofValidationAppendixMethods()
.acsCytofValidationValidateComparisonTable(
  manual_comparison_tbl,
  requiredMethods = c(validation_methods, appendix_methods)
)
# The saved table also holds F-beta at its published defaults, reported in the
# appendix; the main results leave it out.
manual_comparison_all_tbl <- manual_comparison_tbl
manual_comparison_tbl <- .acsCytofMainComparisonTable(manual_comparison_all_tbl)
```

## Scientific inclusion rules

The raw-frequency plots show automated against manual background-subtracted
frequencies for every matched population and cytokine. The correlation outputs
follow the manuscript eligibility rule before calculating Pearson correlation
(PCC) and concordance correlation (CCC): within each population/cytokine/stimulus
stratum, the 75th percentile of the manual stimulated frequency must exceed
three times the larger of 0.01% and the median manual unstimulated frequency,
and the 75th percentile of the manual background-subtracted frequency must
exceed 0.02%. The heatmaps omit the non-secreted-protein (`p4`) stimulation,
matching the manuscript-style display. One set of heatmaps is restricted to
CD4, CD8 and TCRgd T cells and another uses every matched population. This
keeps the original manuscript comparison available while also showing the
additional populations in the current benchmark.

## Frequency-error coverage and donor uncertainty

Manual gating is an imperfect reference, so agreement is not proof of biological
accuracy. Analysis 9b provides absolute frequency-error and relative-error figures
for each stimulus. Absolute error includes zero manual net frequencies; the current
manual and automated net frequencies are truncated at zero after subtraction.
relative error needs a positive manual net frequency, and very small denominators
can dominate it. The table reports matched-row and exclusion denominators.

```{r}
#| label: validation-error-coverage
#| echo: false
#| results: asis
if (isTRUE(run_plots)) {
  .analysis_report_table(.acsCytofManualSummaryTable(manual_comparison_tbl),
    c(fig_key, "validation-error-coverage.csv"),
    "Matched-row, failed, scored and exclusion denominators by stratum.", path_root = root_dir)
}
```

These 95% percentile intervals estimate between-donor uncertainty of mean absolute
frequency and relative errors. All tubes belonging to a donor, including their
shared already-subtracted control, are resampled together using the same donor
draws across stimuli and methods. Finite successful estimates determine the mean;
relative error also requires a positive manual net frequency. Intervals are missing
with fewer than two contributing donors. The bootstrap does not quantify possible
bias or uncertainty in manual gating itself.

```{r}
#| label: validation-donor-uncertainty
#| echo: false
#| results: asis
if (isTRUE(run_plots)) {
  .analysis_report_table(.acsCytofManualUncertainty(manual_comparison_tbl),
    c(fig_key, "validation-donor-uncertainty.csv"),
    "Donor-bootstrap intervals for mean frequency and relative errors.", path_root = root_dir)
}
```

## Results

### Correlation table

```{r}
#| label: correlation-table
#| echo: false
#| results: asis
correlation_tbl <- .acsCytofValidationCorrelationTable(manual_comparison_tbl)
if (isTRUE(run_plots)) {
  .analysis_report_table(correlation_tbl, c(fig_key, "validation-correlations.csv"),
    "Eligible-stratum PCC and CCC with matched-row and exclusion counts.", path_root = root_dir)
}
```

### Unconditional percentiles of signed relative error by stimulus

These figures keep stimuli separate and include every finite signed relative
error, including exact agreement at zero. Relative error is (automated - manual)
/ manual and requires a positive manual net frequency; failed or undefined
estimates remain in the coverage table. Manual gating is an imperfect reference.
Each population panel shows each method's median (solid) and 10th and 90th
percentiles (dotted), with cytokine on the x axis.
Quantiles are computed on raw errors before the signed display transformation.

Donor-bootstrap intervals carry all tubes for a donor together, using common
draws across methods, stimuli and strata. They describe between-donor uncertainty,
not uncertainty in manual gating, and are retained in every render.

```{r}
#| label: validation-signed-percentiles-by-stimulus
#| echo: false
#| results: asis
if (isTRUE(run_plots)) {
  manual_percentiles_by_stimulus <- .acsCytofManualSignedPercentiles(
    manual_comparison_tbl, group_cols = c("method", "pop", "cyt", "stim")
  )
  for (stimulus in unique(as.character(manual_percentiles_by_stimulus$stim))) {
    .analysis_heading(paste("Stimulus:", stimulus), 4)
    for (method in validation_methods) {
      .analysis_heading(paste("Method:", .acsCytofValidationMethodLabels()[[method]]), 5)
      rows <- manual_percentiles_by_stimulus |>
        dplyr::filter(.data$stim == .env$stimulus, .data$method == .env$method)
      p <- .simBandwidthSignedPercentilePlot(
        rows, x = "cyt", x_label = "Cytokine", mcse = TRUE, percentiles = "tails",
        facet = ggplot2::facet_wrap(~pop, scales = "free_y")
      )
      .analysis_print_save_fig(p,
        file.path(.analysis_fig_dir(
          c(fig_key, "signed_percentiles_by_stimulus", stimulus, method), root_dir),
          "manual-comparison-signed-percentiles.png"), height = 22)
      .analysis_report_table(rows |>
        dplyr::select(method, pop, cyt, stim, dplyr::starts_with("n_"),
          dplyr::starts_with("bootstrap_coverage_"), dplyr::starts_with("interval_available_")),
        c(fig_key, "signed_percentiles_by_stimulus", stimulus, paste0(method, ".csv")),
        "Donor-bootstrap validity for unconditional percentiles by stimulus.", path_root = root_dir)
    }
  }
}
```

### Validation figures

```{r}
#| label: save-validation-figures
#| include: false
if (isTRUE(run_plots)) {
  # The figure directory is swapped in whole, so it must not be pre-created.
  path_dir_save <- .analysis_fig_dir(
    c(fig_key, "validation_figures"), root_dir,
    create = FALSE
  )
  .acsCytofValidationSavePlots(
    comparisonTbl = manual_comparison_all_tbl,
    pathDirSave = path_dir_save
  )
}
```

Each figure shows one method. Scatterplots also have a separate figure for each population. The saved figures also cover $F_{\beta}$ at its default settings (see the appendix).

### Raw background-subtracted frequencies

Manual background-subtracted frequency (%) is on the horizontal axis and automated frequency (%) on the vertical axis. Colours and shapes identify stimuli. Each population has its own figure with cytokine panels; both axis ranges differ between panels. Points closer to the identity line indicate closer agreement; horizontal and vertical lines mark zero frequency.

```{r}
#| label: acs-validation-scatter
#| echo: false
#| results: asis
if (isTRUE(run_plots)) {
  for (method in validation_methods) {
    .analysis_heading(
      paste0("Method: ", .acsCytofValidationMethodLabels()[[method]]), 4
    )
    method_rows <- manual_comparison_tbl |> dplyr::filter(.data$method == .env$method)
    for (population in unique(as.character(method_rows$pop))) {
      .analysis_heading(paste("Population:", population), 5)
      .analysis_print_fig(
        .acsCytofValidationPlotScatter(
          method_rows |> dplyr::filter(.data$pop == .env$population), method
        )
      )
    }
  }
}
```

### Correlation heatmaps for CD4, CD8 and TCRgd T cells

Cytokines run across columns and the three T-cell populations across rows, with panels for stimuli. Colour and text show Pearson or concordance correlation for each method after applying the eligibility rules. Values closer to one indicate stronger agreement. Excluded strata are left white without a label; `NA` marks eligible strata whose correlation is unavailable. Blank positions can also have no matched stratum.

```{r}
#| label: thesis-correlation-heatmaps
#| include: false
if (isTRUE(run_plots)) {
  thesis_heatmap_dir <- .analysis_project_dir(
    "output-thesis", c("results", "qmd10", "heatmaps"), root_dir
  )
  # Thesis F-beta uses every cell, including exact zeros (cached fbeta_default).
  thesis_correlation_tbl <- .acsCytofValidationCorrelationTable(manual_comparison_all_tbl)
  .acsCytofReplaceDir(thesis_heatmap_dir, function(stage) {
    # Preserve the independently generated F1 figures and coverage tables.
    existing <- list.files(thesis_heatmap_dir, full.names = TRUE)
    if (length(existing)) stopifnot(all(file.copy(existing, stage, recursive = TRUE)))
    palette_dirs <- c(standard = "", midpoint_0_5 = "palette-midpoint-0.5", viridis = "palette-viridis")
    for (palette in names(palette_dirs)) {
      for (real_only in c(TRUE, FALSE)) {
        for (metric in c("pcc", "ccc")) {
          .analysis_save_thesis_fig(
            .acsCytofThesisPlotCorrelation(
              thesis_correlation_tbl, metric, real_only, palette = palette
            ),
            file.path(stage, palette_dirs[[palette]], paste0(
              metric, "-stacked-", if (real_only) "real-pops" else "all-pops"
            )),
            height = if (real_only) 120 else 155
          )
        }
      }
    }
  })
}
```

Thesis exports include the original red-blue scale and two companions: blue at
zero or below, white at 0.5 and red at one (`palette-midpoint-0.5/`); and the
Analysis 7 viridis scale (`palette-viridis/`). The companions outline eligible tiles so pale
values remain distinct from excluded blanks. Thick lines divide methods.
All versions retain signed correlations and the same -1 to 1 legend; colour
saturates at the low endpoint below zero in the companions.

The table compares the displayed eligible strata for T cells, B cells and NK

```{r}
#| label: thesis-ccc-comparison-summary
```


### Cell agreement with the manual-frequency reference

For each donor, stimulation, population and cytokine, we place a reference gate
on the stimulated expression so the fraction strictly above it is closest to the
manual stimulated frequency minus its matched manual control frequency. Negative
missing or above-100% net frequencies have no attainable reference and remain unscored. Tied values
stay together; equally close counts use the lower gate. The reference selects the
highest-expression cells and does not recover the original manual cell labels.

We compare each method's saved final base gate on these same cells using
$F_1 = 2TP/(2TP + FP + FN)$. No additional background subtraction is applied to
the predicted cell set. Both sets empty gives an undefined score; one empty set
gives zero. Failed gates remain missing. Heatmap values are mean per-tube F₁
scores with equal donor weight within each stratum. Median and 10th-percentile
companions use the same finite per-tube scores. All use the same manual signal
eligibility rules as the correlation figures and omitting `p4`. Coverage tables
report failed, undefined and scored tubes, invalid references and missing saved
audit counts. Reconstructed gates must match saved positive counts and stimulated
frequencies.
White unlabelled tiles are excluded;
`NA` marks eligible strata without a score. Thesis figures use all-cell F-beta.

```{r}
#| label: acs-validation-f1-heatmaps
#| echo: false
#| results: asis
if (isTRUE(run_plots)) {
  path_f1_gs <- projr::projr_path_get(
    "cache", "acs_cytof", "gs", format = "absolute", create = FALSE
  )
  f1_tubes <- .acsCytofF1Table(manual_comparison_all_tbl, path_f1_gs)
  f1_summary <- .acsCytofF1Summary(f1_tubes)
  .analysis_report_table(f1_tubes, c(fig_key, "f1-per-tube.csv"),
    "Reference gates, attainable frequencies and cell confusion counts.", path_root = root_dir)
  .analysis_report_table(
    dplyr::bind_rows(f1_summary, attr(f1_summary, "excludedStrata")),
    c(fig_key, "f1-coverage.csv"),
    "Mean per-tube F1 scores and eligibility/failure coverage.", path_root = root_dir
  )
  for (real_only in c(TRUE, FALSE)) {
    for (method in validation_methods) {
      .analysis_heading(paste(.acsCytofValidationMethodLabels()[[method]],
        if (real_only) "— T cells" else "— all matched populations"), 4)
      .analysis_print_fig(.acsCytofValidationPlotCorrelation(
        f1_summary, method, "f1", real_only
      ))
    }
  }
  .acsCytofReplaceDir(file.path(thesis_heatmap_dir, "f1"), function(stage) {
    utils::write.csv(f1_tubes, file.path(stage, "f1-per-tube.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
    utils::write.csv(
      dplyr::bind_rows(f1_summary, attr(f1_summary, "excludedStrata")),
      file.path(stage, "f1-coverage.csv"), row.names = FALSE
    )
    f1_fields <- c(mean = "f1", median = "f1_median", q10 = "f1_q10")
    f1_titles <- c(mean = "Mean F1 score", median = "Median F1 score", q10 = "10th percentile F1 score")
    for (statistic in names(f1_fields)) {
      plot_summary <- f1_summary
      plot_summary$f1 <- f1_summary[[f1_fields[[statistic]]]]
      for (real_only in c(TRUE, FALSE)) {
        p <- .acsCytofThesisPlotCorrelation(plot_summary, "f1", real_only)
        f1_scale <- p$scales$get_scales("fill")
        f1_scale$name <- f1_titles[[statistic]]
        .analysis_save_thesis_fig(
          p, file.path(stage, paste0(
            "f1-", if (statistic == "mean") "" else paste0(statistic, "-"),
            "stacked-", if (real_only) "real-pops" else "all-pops"
          )), height = if (real_only) 120 else 155
        )
      }
    }
  })
}
```

### F1 comparison summary

This table compares mean finite per-tube F1 scores. Manual net frequency is used
once to infer a reference gate; the score then compares the two positive cell
sets in the same stimulated tube, without further background subtraction.

```{r}
#| label: thesis-f1-comparison-summary
#| echo: false
#| results: asis
if (isTRUE(run_plots) && exists("f1_summary")) {
  f1_comparison_summary <- .acsCytofCccSummary(f1_summary, metric = "f1")
  for (part in c("counts", "coverage", "method_coverage", "strata")) {
    .analysis_report_table(
      f1_comparison_summary[[part]],
      c(fig_key, paste0("f1-comparison-", part, ".csv")),
      paste("F1 comparison", part), path_root = root_dir, quiet = TRUE
    )
  }
  .analysis_md_show(
    .acsCytofCccSummaryMarkdown(f1_comparison_summary),
    file.path(.analysis_project_dir(
      "output-thesis", c("results", "qmd10", "tables"), root_dir
    ), "f1-comparison.md")
  )
}
```

### Stacked frequency scatter plots

Thesis exports stack methods within each population in both 2×3 and 1×6
cytokine panels, and stack populations within each method in 1×6 panels.
These use all-cell F-beta and the existing scatter cohorts and stimulation colours.

```{r}
#| label: thesis-stacked-scatter
#| include: false
if (isTRUE(run_plots)) {
  stacked_scatter_dir <- .analysis_project_dir(
    "output-thesis", c("results", "qmd10", "scatter"), root_dir
  )
  .acsCytofReplaceDir(stacked_scatter_dir, function(stacked_scatter_dir) {
    for (population in unique(as.character(manual_comparison_all_tbl$pop))) {
      population_key <- gsub("[^A-Za-z0-9_.-]+", "_", population)
      for (columns in c(3L, 6L)) {
        stacked_scatter <- .acsCytofStackedScatter(
          manual_comparison_all_tbl, population = population, ncol = columns
        )
        .analysis_save_thesis_fig(
          stacked_scatter$plot,
          file.path(stacked_scatter_dir, paste0("methods-stacked-", if (columns == 3L) "2x3" else "1x6"), population_key),
          height = stacked_scatter$height, width = stacked_scatter$width
        )
      }
    }
    for (method in c("stimgate", "fbeta_default", "tailgate")) {
      stacked_scatter <- .acsCytofStackedScatter(manual_comparison_all_tbl, method = method)
      .analysis_save_thesis_fig(
        stacked_scatter$plot,
        file.path(stacked_scatter_dir, "populations-stacked-1x6", method),
        height = stacked_scatter$height, width = stacked_scatter$width
      )
    }
  })
}
```

### Population-grid frequency scatter plots

Alternatives to the stacked plots: every population in one figure (rows
populations, columns cytokines), with larger outlined points. One set of
figures shows all three methods (colour method, shape stimulation); the other
draws one figure per method (colour and shape stimulation). Each comes with a
least-squares line per stimulation (`fit-per-stim`), one line per panel
(`fit-per-panel`; per method in the all-method figures) or no lines (`no-fit`).
Failed thresholds are left out, and the grey diagonal is $y = x$.

```{r}
#| label: thesis-scatter-alt
#| include: false
if (isTRUE(run_plots)) {
  scatter_alt_dir <- .analysis_project_dir(
    "output-thesis", c("results", "qmd10", "scatter-grid"), root_dir
  )
  scatter_alt_fits <- c(stim = "fit-per-stim", panel = "fit-per-panel", none = "no-fit")
  .acsCytofReplaceDir(scatter_alt_dir, function(scatter_alt_dir) {
    for (fit in names(scatter_alt_fits)) {
      for (method in list(NULL, "stimgate", "fbeta_default", "tailgate")) {
        scatter_alt <- .acsCytofScatterAlt(manual_comparison_all_tbl, method = method, fit = fit)
        .analysis_save_thesis_fig(
          scatter_alt$plot,
          file.path(
            scatter_alt_dir, if (is.null(method)) "all-methods" else method,
            scatter_alt_fits[[fit]]
          ),
          height = scatter_alt$height, width = scatter_alt$width
        )
      }
    }
  })
}
```

## Appendix: $F_{\beta}$ at default settings

The main results use $F_{\beta}$ as adapted for the CyTOF data in Analysis 9b:
cells with an expression of exactly zero are removed before the gate is
estimated. Here $F_{\beta}$ uses its published defaults on every cell instead
($\beta=0.8$, `theta = 2`, `width = 10` and pdfs that integrate to one). The
eligibility rules and heatmap layout match the main results. Tailgate's
alternative settings, including its automatic-tolerance and cytoUtils
defaults, are compared in Analysis 9a.

```{r}
#| label: appendix-correlation-table
#| echo: false
#| results: asis
appendix_correlation_tbl <- .acsCytofValidationCorrelationTable(
  manual_comparison_all_tbl |>
    dplyr::filter(.data$method %in% appendix_methods)
)
if (isTRUE(run_plots)) {
  .analysis_report_table(appendix_correlation_tbl,
    c(fig_key, "validation-correlations-default-settings.csv"),
    "Eligible-stratum PCC and CCC for F-beta at default settings.",
    path_root = root_dir)
}
```

```{r}
    for (metric in c("pcc", "ccc")) {
      .analysis_heading(
        if (metric == "pcc") "Pearson correlation" else "Concordance correlation",
        5
      )
      .analysis_print_fig(.acsCytofValidationPlotCorrelation(
        correlationTbl = appendix_correlation_tbl,
        method = method,
        metric = metric,
        realPopulationsOnly = TRUE
      ))
    }
  }
}
```

```{r}

      .analysis_print_fig(.acsCytofValidationPlotCorrelation(
        correlationTbl = appendix_correlation_tbl,
        method = method,
        metric = metric,
        realPopulationsOnly = FALSE
      ))
    }
  }
}
```
